source.title: Understanding and Mitigating Gender Bias in LLMs via Interpretable Neuron Editing

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies neuron roles and edits neurons to mitigate gender bias, but it does not test polysemanticity or rely on a finding about polysemantic neurons.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure how often neurons respond to unrelated inputs or compare explanations of polysemantic neurons. The rows below capture a related but different result: effects of masking selected neurons on other task performance. Gender-bias mitigation benchmark results are not rows because they evaluate the editing method, not polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: The study locates gender-bias neurons and general neurons in Llama-7B and edits them to reduce bias. It never measures whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, how common polysemantic neurons are, or what causes them. The general neurons that help both gender bias and common tasks are a related multi-role finding. It is not a polysemanticity measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors identify gender neurons and general neurons as contributors to gender bias. They find general neurons affect other tasks by changing higher-layer neuron coefficients. Their interpretable neuron editing reduces bias while preserving common-task performance across five LLMs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses neuron attribution and causal masking to study and edit gender-bias mechanisms; it does not apply a method for measuring polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: Two early-layer neurons (L2 N7003, N4090) are activated by the <start> token and are important for gender-bias predictions. Masking them collapses RACE and arithmetic accuracy, which the authors attribute to disrupted coefficients of higher-layer neurons. The authors say these neurons show little interpretability in vocabulary projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some early-layer FFN neurons in LLMs serve broad general roles, so ablating them disrupts many unrelated tasks.

record.problems: The neuron-role analysis is conducted on Llama-7B and uses specific cases; the paper notes that its interpretability assumptions, including projecting neurons into vocabulary space, may be approximate. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the cited results.
record.rows_left_out: Gender-bias benchmark and method-comparison results in Tables 4–5 and 11–13 are omitted because they evaluate debiasing methods rather than polysemanticity or neuron responses to unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: No share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and no layer breakdown.
No test of initialization, regularization or noise as causes.
No comparison of architectures or activation functions.
No reanalysis of canonical polysemantic neurons.

record.verdict_notes: There are no claims about polysemanticity. Tables 4-5 and 11-13 are method comparisons and are rightly left out. The relation could also be T6/cites_only, since Templeton 2024 is cited only for coefficient-based selection.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifiers or vision neurons are studied.
The paper does not measure the share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, or variation by layer.
No test of superposition or feature-to-neuron capacity pressure.
No test of initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity.
No comparison of activation functions or architecture for polysemanticity.
The paper does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons with improved tools or test whether their inputs share a feature.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for classifying polysemanticity.

rows.subject: Llama-7B
rows.operation_detail: Masked general neurons ffn L2 N7003 and ffn L2 N4090 by setting their parameters to zero.

conditions.value: ffn L2 N7003 and ffn L2 N4090

rows.note: Ablation of the two selected general neurons reduced reading-comprehension accuracy.
rows.check: Masking two general neurons lowers RACE accuracy (63.5% to 31.5%). This is an ablation importance result, not a measure of neurons responding to unrelated inputs. The text says it masks the 'top two gender neurons' while naming the general neurons ffn L2 N7003/N4090, an internal inconsistency.

rows.subject: Llama-7B
rows.operation_detail: Masked general neurons ffn L2 N7003 and ffn L2 N4090 by setting their parameters to zero.

conditions.value: ffn L2 N7003 and ffn L2 N4090

rows.note: The paper also reports that, for the case “3+5=”, the prediction changed from “8” to “1” after masking these neurons.
rows.check: Same ablation, measured on Arithmetic (51.9% to 7.5%). It is not a polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: Llama-7B
rows.operation_detail: Edited a gender-related neuron, ffn L4 N2026; the text describes its effect on coefficient scores in the arithmetic case.
rows.value: prediction remains “8”; coefficient scores of ffn L11 N2258 and ffn L12 N4072 change by an average of 0.8%
rows.note: The paper contrasts editing this gender-related neuron with masking the two general neurons.
rows.check: This is a single-case contrast (editing ffn L4 N2026 keeps the prediction '8'), with no polysemanticity measure. 'absent' is not meaningful relative to any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
